heroHeadline: Day 677: CJNG Breaks Alliance with Chapitos in Baja California — New War Front Opening; Two Colombian 'Los Rusos' Operatives Arrested in Mexicali; US Enforcement Pivots to CDN as Sinaloa Fractures
heroSubtitle: 677 days of cartel civil war — May 31, 2026: CJNG has formally broken its alliance with Los Chapitos in Baja California, with state security forces confirming both organizations have entered open conflict over control of Tijuana, Mexicali, and Ensenada — the most definitive post-Mencho territorial rupture yet. Simultaneously, Proceso reported two Colombian nationals linked to La Mayiza's 'Los Rusos' armed wing were arrested in the Mexicali Valley (Darwin Ferney 'El Zarco' and Alexander), with two stolen Arizona-plated vehicles seized. With their external CJNG military patron now actively contesting their BC positions, Los Chapitos face simultaneous fronts: war with La Mayiza in Sinaloa, security force pressure (13-to-1 arrest ratio per Infobae May 27), and CJNG-BC hostilities. El Financiero (May 30) consolidated the US court calendar: El Mayo EDNY sentencing July 20 (defense memo due July 6), Ovidio NDIL July 27, Joaquín Aug 31, Gerardo Mérida first SDNY hearing ~June 1–3. US enforcement is simultaneously pivoting to Cártel del Noreste (CDN) as Sinaloa fractures — 12 CDN operators now under active US targeting (Infobae/Noticias Latam, May 30–31). El Chinacate (Isaí Martínez Zepeda) held at Altiplano; US has ~28 days remaining to file formal extradition request. Three SDNY-indicted FGR fugitives — Contreras Núñez, Dionisio Hipólito, Valenzuela Millán — enter Day 32 unaccounted for. La Mayiza ~90% territorial control; 13,300+ federal troops under interim Governor Bonilla Valverde. Running toll: ~2,425+ homicides (Noroeste) / 3,000+ (WSJ) since September 9, 2024; ~5,800 disappearances (NGO Sabuesos Unidas AC).
